q: Addition polymerisation of monomers proceeds mainly in which three mechanistic steps?
why: Chain-growth addition polymerisation occurs via initiation of the double bond, propagation of the chain, then termination.

q: Condensation polymerisation differs from addition polymerisation mainly because it
o: Needs only one type of monomer
Involves loss of a small molecule like water at each step
why: In condensation polymerisation, bifunctional monomers link with elimination of a small molecule such as water at each step.

q: Nylon-6,6 is formed by condensation of hexamethylenediamine with
why: Nylon-6,6 is a polyamide formed from hexamethylenediamine and adipic acid, releasing water at each amide bond.

q: Buna-S, used to manufacture vehicle tyres, is a copolymer of
why: Buna-S is formed by copolymerising 1,3-butadiene with styrene, giving a tough synthetic rubber.

q: Natural rubber is chemically described as
o: A copolymer of butadiene and isoprene
why: Natural rubber is a 1,4-addition polymer of isoprene with cis configuration, which gives it its elastic property.

q: Vulcanisation of rubber involves heating raw rubber with sulphur to
o: Form sulphur cross-links between polymer chains, increasing strength
why: Sulphur forms cross-links (bridges) between rubber chains during vulcanisation, improving strength and elasticity.

q: PHBV, a biodegradable copolyester used in packaging and sutures, is broken down naturally by
why: Biodegradable polymers like PHBV contain ester linkages that microorganisms can hydrolyse into simple, non-toxic products.

why: Nylon-2-nylon-6 is a copolymer formed from glycine and amino caproic acid, making it biodegradable.
